subject: FintechCo — followup on logging & PII redaction
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: FintechCo — logging & PII redaction follow-up

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the discovery call today — really helpful to understand the flows you’re most concerned about (loan origination API requests, KYC enrichment, and the webhook-based transaction alerts). Per your ask, I’ve summarized Redwood’s current capabilities on logging controls and sensitive-data redaction below, plus a proposed next steps checklist so we can get your security and engineering teams comfortable.

Summary of controls relevant to FintechCo:
- Request/response logging: by default we capture structured request/response metadata (timestamp, model id, latency, token counts) and maintain optional full request/response bodies for a configurable retention window.
- PII redaction: we support configurable redaction at ingestion and at persistent logging. Redaction rules can be regex-based, named-entity-based (SSN, credit card, email), or field-path-based for JSON payloads.
- Headers & trace ids: headers and trace identifiers are included in audit records by default but can be excluded or hashed. We recommend hashing trace IDs when you need correlation without exposing raw request IDs.
- Masking vs removal: Redwood lets you mask (e.g., replace with <REDACTED>) or remove fields entirely. Masking preserves schema for debugging while removal yields stronger privacy guarantees.
- Data residency & retention: logs can be stored in-region (US/EU) for Dedicated/Private deployments and retention is configurable per-route (default 30 days, configurable to 0/90/365+).
- Audit & access controls: role-based access controls for logs, immutable audit trails, and integration with customer KMS for endpoint encryption.

Examples we shared on the call (redaction snippets you can apply):
- Header exclusion: set log_config.exclude_headers = ["Authorization", "Cookie"]
- Trace ID hashing: log_config.hash_fields = ["x-trace-id"] with SHA256 salt stored in your KMS
- JSON path redaction: log_config.redact_paths = ["$.user.ssn", "$.payment.card_number"]

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll drop a redaction_config.yaml you can review (attached) with the examples above and a proposed default set for FintechCo.
2) If OK, we’d get a quick 30-min session with your infra/security team to walk the YAML and the minimal config changes to further mask trace ids and headers.
3) We can provide a scoped SOC2 artifact bundle and a short demo on Private deployment options if you need in-region storage — attached is a redacted SOC2 summary.

Questions for you:
- Do you need retention <30 days for any specific route?
- Are there internal tracing/observability IDs that must never leave your VPC (we can configure a no-export rule)?

I’ve cc’d Rishi (AE) to coordinate scheduling and Neha (security) to jump in on the technical call if helpful.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

Thanks Marissa — this is a great summary. A couple of clarifying items from our security and infra teams after a quick read: 

1) We can accept masked values for debugging, but we need to ensure deterministic hashing for trace correlation across systems (i.e., same input -> same hash). Is the hash salt controllable by us?
2) For webhook delivery failures we’d like to capture response codes and short bodies (for triage) but must guarantee that any card numbers, SSNs, or full account numbers are not persisted. Can you confirm the best-practice config?
3) Data residency: we operate primarily in us-west-2 and need logs to stay in-region for the lifecycle of the deal. Is that available on the hosted path or would we need Dedicated/Private?

Also, Rajiv (cc’d) will own the security review — he’ll want the SOC2 bundle and the exact redaction_config.yaml to run through our compliance scanner. Can we get the yaml in a format our scanner can ingest without manual edits?

Can we schedule the 30-min technical session next week (week of Dec 7)? Prefer Tue/Wed mornings PST.

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FintechCo — logging & PII redaction follow-up

Emily — great questions, answered inline below.

1) Deterministic hashing
Yes — customers can control the hash salt via their KMS (we support passing a KMS-wrapped salt for determinism). We recommend using HMAC-SHA256 with a customer-managed key so the same input hashes identically across services without exposing the raw id.

2) Webhook failure bodies
Best practice we’ve seen:
- Capture status_code and a 256-char truncated body for triage.
- Apply path-based redaction to any JSON payloads and regex-based redaction for plaintext logs. Example config:
  log_config.truncate_body = 256
  log_config.redact_paths = ["$.payment.card_number", "$.user.ssn"]
  log_config.redact_regex = ["\\b\\d{13,19}\\b"]  # common card number regex
This preserves the ability to debug without persisting sensitive values.

3) Data residency
Hosted API currently stores logs in multi-region US buckets and cannot guarantee single-region-only retention on the standard hosted tier. For strict in-region controls you’d need Dedicated or Private, both of which support us-west-2 residency for logs and data. We can scope an estimate for Dedicated capacity in the same call.

Scanner-ready YAML
I attached a scanner-ready redaction_config.yaml that follows your vendor scanner schema (JSON-schema compatible). If you have sample output from the scanner that flags any fields we can iterate quickly.

Scheduling
Rishi will send a calendar invite for Tue 8 Dec at 10:00 AM PST unless that conflicts — does that work for you and Rajiv?

- Marissa: confirm Dedicated pricing estimate if FintechCo wants single-region retention
- Neha: join the technical call for deeper redaction & KMS discussion

Thanks — happy to jump on the call and walk through the yaml if needed.
